LESSON: READING 3.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.2: Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading, part of Strand 3 in Grade 8 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: Why should we read extensively? 2. Why is it important to take care of wildlife? 3. What can be done to avoid road accidents involving wild animals?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. explain vocabulary related to the theme for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. paraphrase the main idea from a text for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. embrace reading as a source of acquiring information.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. explain vocabulary related to the theme for effective communication,

   Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. paraphrase the main idea from a text for comprehension,

   Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. embrace reading as a source of acquiring information.

   Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read texts related to safety of wild animals on our roads (for example, road signs, being cautious, animal ambulance),

2. identify vocabulary related to the theme- wildlife,

3. team up with peers to play a language game to match the vocabulary identified to their meaning,

4. work with peers to construct sentences using the vocabulary identified,

5. paraphrase the main idea from the text,

6. share the summary with peers for review,

7. collaborate with peers to prepare a creative mosaic of a wild animal of choice and display during the interclass exhibitions. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read texts related to safety of wild animals on our roads (for example, road signs, being cautious, animal ambulance),
2. identify vocabulary related to the theme- wildlife,
3. team up with peers to play a language game to match the vocabulary identified to their meaning,
4. work with peers to construct sentences using the vocabulary identified,
5. paraphrase the main idea from the text,
6. share the summary with peers for review,
7. collaborate with peers to prepare a creative mosaic of a wild animal of choice and display during the interclass exhibitions. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to Learn: This is promoted as the learner is motivated to learn continuously by sharing the summary with peers for

review.

Values:
• Responsibility: The learner offers leadership and guidance when playing a language game to match the vocabulary.

• Respect: This is nurtured as the learner displays patience with peers when playing a language game to match the vocabulary

identified to their meaning.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Animal welfare education: This is promoted as the learner reads about preservation of wildlife.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate knowledge gained in reading on preservation of wildlife to their learning of living things in

Integrated Science.

Main points to remember:

1. explain vocabulary related to the theme for effective communication,
2. paraphrase the main idea from a text for comprehension,
3. embrace reading as a source of acquiring information.

Remember the key question: Why should we read extensively? 2. Why is it important to take care of wildlife? 3. What can be done to avoid road accidents involving wild animals?
